- id: f001
  description: 'Seed mechanism (usbip_recv_iso, demonstration only, never reportable): (1) Untrusted source: a peer-controlled count (urb->number_of_packets) copied verbatim from a remote protocol message (ret_submit unpack) into a shared kernel object before any validation — the attacker is the remote endpoint of a device/virtual-bus protocol, not a local user. (2) Missing guarantee: no bounds clamp of the count against the protocol maximum (USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS existed but was only enforced on the submit/other-direction path — asymmetric validation), and no overflow-checked sizing (manual `int size = np * sizeof(*iso)` in 32-bit instead of kcalloc/array_size/struct_size). (3) Unsafe use/state transition: the truncated product goes to kzalloc, then a per-element loop runs np iterations of recv+copy into the undersized heap buffer; additionally, the early-error return leaves the poisoned count set in urb->number_of_packets, which the URB completion path (processcompl) later iterates. (4) Consequence: remotely triggerable kernel heap buffer overflow (OOB write) plus OOB read on the completion/error-unwind path — memory corruption, crash/DoS, potential privilege escalation. Transferable invariant: whenever a length/count/size quantity crosses a trust boundary into kernel state, three guarantees must hold — the count is range-checked at parse time against a known maximum, every buffer-size computation derived from it is overflow-checked, and no failure path leaves the unchecked count in shared state for later iteration. BRANCHES: branch1=alloc-multiply-overflow (32-bit count*element-size or count+offset/shift arithmetic assigned to int/uint and passed to kmalloc/kzalloc/vmalloc/memdup followed by an element-indexed copy/recv loop, where the multiplier is untrusted — hunt the arithmetic-to-allocator-to-loop chain in driver and fs code within one snapshot); branch2=unclamped-wire-count (deserialization/unpack/recvmsg/netlink-nla/ioctl-in paths that copy count/length/nr_fields from the wire or userspace into kernel objects with no range check, especially where a sibling path of the same protocol enforces a MAX limit but the mirror path does not — asymmetric validation between paired directions); branch3=error-unwind-poisoned-count (early-return/failure/teardown paths that leave an attacker-controlled count/length/actual_size field set in a shared object — urb, request, skb, sgl, iovec — that a completion handler, cleanup routine, or status-out path later iterates, causing OOB access during error handling); branch4=peer-trusted-transport (kernel-side clients/servers of remote or virtual device transports — network-exported bus, virtual HCD, guest-host, remote-storage/remote-fs reply handlers — that allocate or loop based on peer-supplied response fields without cross-checking locally-known limits, i.e., trust-boundary consumption of a remote peer''s reply, identified by mechanism rather than subsystem name); seed names (usbip, recv_iso, number_of_packets) must never be used as the finding itself.'

    coverage_gap=drivers/usb/storage/transport.c us->current_urb->actual_length consumers and drivers/staging/gpib bulk_urb->actual_length consumers were identified but not deep-read; they are sync-URB style paths where the same HCD bound applies.

- id: f051
  description: |-
    intent=i052 snapshot=s13 branch=unclamped-wire-count status=complete
    finding location=net/bluetooth/hci_event.c:4926-4945 confidence=high conclusion=HCI LE Advertising Report event handler loops on controller-supplied num_reports with zero skb length validation and no per-report bounds on the peer-controlled ev->length advance, unlike sibling handlers that check skb->len - OOB read of event data past the skb.
    finding location=net/bluetooth/hci_event.c:5124-5137 confidence=high conclusion=HCI LE Direct Advertising Report handler walks num_reports controller-supplied fixed-size entries with no skb->len validation unlike sibling count handlers that enforce skb->len coverage - OOB read of up to ~255 entries past the buffer.
    finding location=fs/cifs/misc.c:649-687 confidence=high conclusion=CIFS parse_dfs_referrals trusts server-supplied NumberOfReferrals (le16) with only a <1 check, then walks that many 34-byte referral structs and stores them via kcalloc without ever bounding the count against rsp_size - OOB read of the response buffer.
    finding location=fs/cifs/cifsacl.c:742-756 confidence=high conclusion=CIFS parse_dacl consumes server-supplied num_aces (le32) with no cross-check against the already-validated pdacl->size, walking that many ACEs (each strided by a peer-controlled le16 size) past the response buffer while deriving file mode - OOB read.
    finding location=drivers/md/raid5-ppl.c:829-841 confidence=medium conclusion=raid5-ppl recovery loop iterates on-disk pplhdr->entries_count (u32) with no PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES clamp that the write path enforces at raid5-ppl.c:274, walking a fixed 126-entry page array with crafted pp_size also driving disk I/O - header CRC over the page is the only gate.
    finding location=drivers/net/ethernet/qlogic/netxen/netxen_nic_ctx.c:380-395 confidence=medium conclusion=netxen create_rx_ctx consumes firmware-reply num_rds_rings/num_sds_rings (le16) without checking against the counts it requested, indexing past the small kcalloc'd ring arrays (OOB pointer writes) and past the sized DMA response buffer.
    unresolved location=drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c:611 conclusion=Seed usbip_recv_iso unclamped-count chain confirmed unpatched in s13 at drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c:611-614; excluded from findings by rule - track via the dedicated seed CVE, do not re-report here.
    unresolved location=drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx4/mcg.c:350 conclusion=mlx4 multicast mgm->members_count (&0xffffff, up to 16.7M) from device READ_ENTRY is looped over the fixed ~1020-entry qp[] array with no clamp that write paths enforce - follow up by confirming the cmd-mailbox buffer size vs MLX4_MAX_QP_PER_MGM and whether caps.num_qp_per_mgm can exceed the array.
    coverage_gap=copy_from_user ioctl/netlink nla_parse paths (sound, media, target configfs, block ioctls) named in the intent's broader scope were not swept in this session; only the wire/peer-response le/be count sites were covered.
    coverage_gap=qlcnic_ctx.c:355/364 was seen to contain the identical netxen unclamped num_rds/num_sds_rings pattern but was not independently verified (same firmware trust model, likely same verdict).
    artifact=findings/i052.json

    unresolved location=drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c:473 conclusion=Seed location confirmed unpatched in s12 and excluded by rule; follow up only to confirm it is tracked as the demonstration instance.
    unresolved location=drivers/scsi/esas2r/esas2r_main.c:1443 conclusion=Follow up: read the num_targets_backend consumer loop and check it against the array it indexes (candidate for the same asymmetric-clamp pattern as pmcraid).
    unresolved location=drivers/scsi/qla4xxx/ql4_nx.c:2640 conclusion=Follow up: verify the minidump entry-processing path cannot make the unbounded count loop corrupt state past entry-buffer accounting (MMIO-only loop, likely DoS-grade, not memory R/W).

    coverage_gap=Bluetooth hci_event/hci_mgmt event count fields, 802.15.4/6LoWPAN frame parsers, and AF_ALG/crypto user-socket length paths were not swept in this pass.
    coverage_gap=NFS/AFS/Ceph XDR reply decoders were spot-checked at known count sites (yfsclient ACL sizes, nfs42 xattr/list counts, blocklayout and filelayout counts, ceph split counts) and found bounded, but the remainder of nfs4xdr.c/nfs42xdr.c decode functions were not read line-by-line.

    artifact=findings/i048.json

  description: 'SNAPSHOT=s01; BRANCH=alloc-multiply-overflow; Search only snapshots/s01. Direct structural/API analogue of the seed''s sizing chain: hunt a 32-bit multiply (count*element-size, count+offset, or count<<shift) computed with plain int/unsigned arithmetic from an untrusted count and passed to kmalloc/kzalloc/vmalloc/kmemdup/devm_kzalloc instead of kcalloc/array_size/struct_size, followed by an element-indexed copy/recv/memcpy loop that still trusts the original count, so the truncated product under-allocates and the loop writes past the heap buffer. For each candidate record file:line of the unchecked arithmetic, the allocator call, the consuming loop, and where the count enters from outside the kernel; a negative result must cite the allocator-adjacent arithmetic sites examined.     coverage_gap=drivers/usb/storage/transport.c us->current_urb->actual_length consumers and drivers/staging/gpib bulk_urb->actual_length consumers were identified but not deep-read; they are sync-URB style paths where the same HCD bound applies.

- id: f051
  description: |-
    intent=i052 snapshot=s13 branch=unclamped-wire-count status=complete
    finding location=net/bluetooth/hci_event.c:4926-4945 confidence=high conclusion=HCI LE Advertising Report event handler loops on controller-supplied num_reports with zero skb length validation and no per-report bounds on the peer-controlled ev->length advance, unlike sibling handlers that check skb->len - OOB read of event data past the skb.
    finding location=net/bluetooth/hci_event.c:5124-5137 confidence=high conclusion=HCI LE Direct Advertising Report handler walks num_reports controller-supplied fixed-size entries with no skb->len validation unlike sibling count handlers that enforce skb->len coverage - OOB read of up to ~255 entries past the buffer.
    finding location=fs/cifs/misc.c:649-687 confidence=high conclusion=CIFS parse_dfs_referrals trusts server-supplied NumberOfReferrals (le16) with only a <1 check, then walks that many 34-byte referral structs and stores them via kcalloc without ever bounding the count against rsp_size - OOB read of the response buffer.
    finding location=fs/cifs/cifsacl.c:742-756 confidence=high conclusion=CIFS parse_dacl consumes server-supplied num_aces (le32) with no cross-check against the already-validated pdacl->size, walking that many ACEs (each strided by a peer-controlled le16 size) past the response buffer while deriving file mode - OOB read.
    finding location=drivers/md/raid5-ppl.c:829-841 confidence=medium conclusion=raid5-ppl recovery loop iterates on-disk pplhdr->entries_count (u32) with no PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES clamp that the write path enforces at raid5-ppl.c:274, walking a fixed 126-entry page array with crafted pp_size also driving disk I/O - header CRC over the page is the only gate.
    finding location=drivers/net/ethernet/qlogic/netxen/netxen_nic_ctx.c:380-395 confidence=medium conclusion=netxen create_rx_ctx consumes firmware-reply num_rds_rings/num_sds_rings (le16) without checking against the counts it requested, indexing past the small kcalloc'd ring arrays (OOB pointer writes) and past the sized DMA response buffer.
    unresolved location=drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c:611 conclusion=Seed usbip_recv_iso unclamped-count chain confirmed unpatched in s13 at drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c:611-614; excluded from findings by rule - track via the dedicated seed CVE, do not re-report here.
    unresolved location=drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx4/mcg.c:350 conclusion=mlx4 multicast mgm->members_count (&0xffffff, up to 16.7M) from device READ_ENTRY is looped over the fixed ~1020-entry qp[] array with no clamp that write paths enforce - follow up by confirming the cmd-mailbox buffer size vs MLX4_MAX_QP_PER_MGM and whether caps.num_qp_per_mgm can exceed the array.
    coverage_gap=copy_from_user ioctl/netlink nla_parse paths (sound, media, target configfs, block ioctls) named in the intent's broader scope were not swept in this session; only the wire/peer-response le/be count sites were covered.
    coverage_gap=qlcnic_ctx.c:355/364 was seen to contain the identical netxen unclamped num_rds/num_sds_rings pattern but was not independently verified (same firmware trust model, likely same verdict).
    artifact=findings/i052.json

    unresolved location=drivers/usb/usbip/usbip_common.c:473 conclusion=Seed location confirmed unpatched in s12 and excluded by rule; follow up only to confirm it is tracked as the demonstration instance.
    unresolved location=drivers/scsi/esas2r/esas2r_main.c:1443 conclusion=Follow up: read the num_targets_backend consumer loop and check it against the array it indexes (candidate for the same asymmetric-clamp pattern as pmcraid).
    unresolved location=drivers/scsi/qla4xxx/ql4_nx.c:2640 conclusion=Follow up: verify the minidump entry-processing path cannot make the unbounded count loop corrupt state past entry-buffer accounting (MMIO-only loop, likely DoS-grade, not memory R/W).

    coverage_gap=Bluetooth hci_event/hci_mgmt event count fields, 802.15.4/6LoWPAN frame parsers, and AF_ALG/crypto user-socket length paths were not swept in this pass.
    coverage_gap=NFS/AFS/Ceph XDR reply decoders were spot-checked at known count sites (yfsclient ACL sizes, nfs42 xattr/list counts, blocklayout and filelayout counts, ceph split counts) and found bounded, but the remainder of nfs4xdr.c/nfs42xdr.c decode functions were not read line-by-line.

    artifact=findings/i048.json

  description: 'SNAPSHOT=s01; BRANCH=alloc-multiply-overflow; Search only snapshots/s01. Direct structural/API analogue of the seed''s sizing chain: hunt a 32-bit multiply (count*element-size, count+offset, or count<<shift) computed with plain int/unsigned arithmetic from an untrusted count and passed to kmalloc/kzalloc/vmalloc/kmemdup/devm_kzalloc instead of kcalloc/array_size/struct_size, followed by an element-indexed copy/recv/memcpy loop that still trusts the original count, so the truncated product under-allocates and the loop writes past the heap buffer. For each candidate record file:line of the unchecked arithmetic, the allocator call, the consuming loop, and where the count enters from outside the kernel; a negative result must cite the allocator-adjacent arithmetic sites examined.
